citations.title: Purpose and scope
citations.requirement: Chapter sets minimum requirements for residential services to people with DD. It applies to provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments. Community care residences (Family Care/Skill Development in a private home) are licensed under 10:44B. Head-injury residences fall under 10:44C. Licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Community residence: up to 16 individuals, not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population. Supervised apartment: up to 4 individuals per apartment. Full license: up to one year. Also defines Abuse, Exploitation, Central Registry, Critical information, Direct support professional, Governing authority, Community agency head, Executive director, Behavior support plan, Falsification, Fiduciary capacity, Guardian, Authorization to operate (permits operation past license expiration when an inspection is delayed), Eviction, and Service plan/planning team.

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: (a) Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider plus the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (b) No agency head may be paid or contracted until criminal history clearance under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69; owner/licensee also checked if different from the agency head. (c)(1) Application contents include a table of organization, CVs, owners, 24 months of service history with survey results and plans of correction, penalties/fines record, CPA examination for two fiscal years, and 3 professional references each. (d)(1) 45 days to complete or the application may be denied, with a 6-month bar on reapplying. (g) Written decision within 60 calendar days. (i) The procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, then job descriptions go to DDD. (j) No operation without Office of Licensing authorization. (k) DHS inspection without limitation or notice. (l) Annual on-site inspection. (m) No license after denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance. (n) No license if a final finding of discrimination exists.

citations.title: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee's purposes and a description of its services must be made available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the general public. Other subsections of 2.1 were not read.

citations.title: Development and maintenance of procedure manual
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee develops and implements a written procedure manual. Procedures are reviewed annually. Each procedure is designed on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning. Each has a unique title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities and reporting/recording requirements. (b) Required contents: 1 philosophy; 2 table of organization; 3 Central Registry compliance; 4 New Employee Orientation Checklist; 5 major emergency/evacuation plan, including indoor air below 68F or above 82F for four consecutive hours; 6 medical emergencies with a 9-1-1 call for life-threatening emergencies (Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A); 7 emergency coverage/on-call; 8 unusual incident reporting with a written prohibition on abuse, neglect and exploitation and the obligation to report each allegation; 9 investigations; 10 fiscal management of personal funds; 11 safekeeping of valuables; 12 list and schedule of charges and fees; 13 complaint/grievance procedure with at least two levels, the last involving the licensee or executive director; 14 separate internal communication/critical-information log; 15 admissions per 10:44A-4; 16 confidentiality per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2; 17 medication administration and self-medication; 18 controlled dangerous substance testing of employees (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5); 19 exchange of contact information with involved family/guardians (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6); 20 Child Abuse Registry check; 21 video/audio monitoring of common areas, if applicable; 22 continuous quality improvement system.

citations.title: Implementation of procedure manual
citations.requirement: The section exists per the LII subchapter 2 table of contents. Its operative text was not read. Confirm what it requires for staff access to and implementation of the manual before relying on it.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Personnel requirements, including employee screening. All employees who may contact individuals must comply with the screening requirements. A provider-hosted copy of the 2023 text shows a TB screen (Mantoux 5 TU PPD or IGRA blood test) within one year before or upon starting work, with written results submitted to the licensee. The 2005 text also required annual repeat testing, so confirm the current subsection letter and any repeat interval.

citations.title: Minimum staff qualifications
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee or executive director has a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive DD management experience (at least two supervisory at a senior/administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal/qualitative standards. (b) Residence supervisor has a high school diploma or equivalent plus one year of DD experience. (c) DSPs are 18 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent. (d) DSPs can communicate with the individuals they work with. (e) DSPs can provide the direct assistance or training required. (f) Licensee verifies professional credentials required by law for employed or contracted professionals.

citations.title: Orientation
citations.requirement: The section exists per the LII table of contents. 10:44A-2.2(b)4 requires the New Employee Orientation Checklist to include all of 10:44A-2.6(a)1 through 8. The text of 2.6 was not read, so confirm the eight items before drafting the checklist.

citations.title: Staff training
citations.requirement: (a) Within 90 days of employment each DSP completes Division basic training: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, first aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant entity, each with a valid certificate on file. (b) Medication training and demonstrated competency come before administering any medication, and competency is shown annually. (c) Training in all relevant policies not covered in orientation. (d) Specialized training within 90 days of employment: feeding techniques (feeding tube duties delegated to nursing), mobility devices and transport, seizure/physical/medical needs, mental health needs, and behavior support plans. (e) Training records kept in the administrative office with a curriculum/training plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, and Division-required results. (f) Additional training is allowed without Division approval. (g) Training under (c) is delivered by a qualified trainer.

citations.title: Staff coverage
citations.requirement: (a) A written staff schedule for at least two weeks is available at each residence with full staff names. It shows on-site coverage per the program description, and an in-charge employee for each shift. Temporary agency staff may not be designated in-charge unless all 2.7 training is complete and a written policy states the licensee assumes responsibility and liability. (b) Each required specialized training is completed by at least one person on each shift. (c) Staff need not be on site when no individuals are present, but trained, paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies. (d) Group home/supervised apartment staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs. (e) The staff residence/office of a supervised apartment program is located so response time fits supervision needs. No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A.

citations.title: Records of individuals receiving services
citations.requirement: (a) An individual file is kept for each individual receiving services. (b) Files for group home and supervised apartment residents are kept at the residence. Contents include full name, DOB and sex; Social Security and Medicaid/insurance numbers; and dates of admission, readmission, transfer or discharge. The remaining required contents and any retention period were not read.

citations.title: Individual financial records: personal funds
citations.requirement: The licensee keeps a written record of all financial arrangements and transactions involving individuals' entrusted funds. Each individual and guardian has access to it on request, and copies are provided on request. The 2005 text also required the licensee to manage funds so as not to jeopardize benefit entitlements. Confirm the current subsection.

citations.title: Advocacy and rights: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Services recognize that people with disabilities have the same rights as other citizens, and exercising rights is never a cause for retribution. (b) Licensee complies with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (c) Staff are familiar with and observe the rights listed in the Division's rights document. The licensee provides the rights document and gets acknowledgments on admission. (d) Individuals receive training and support to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because an individual has a guardian or family. (e) The licensee uses a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A. House rules involve the affected individuals, are necessary for order, and do not infringe on others' rights.

citations.title: Rules governing a residence
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and the 2023 subchapter 3 range (3.1 to 3.3). Snippets show house rules must involve the affected individuals, be necessary to promote order, and not infringe on others' rights. The current text was not read, so confirm subsection lettering.

citations.title: Self-advocacy
citations.requirement: Title seen only in the 2005 rule text. The current operative text was not read. Confirm what it requires for supporting self-advocacy before relying on it.

citations.title: Pre-admission and admission
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and in the 2023 subchapter 4 range (4.1 to 4.3). 10:44A-2.2(b)15 requires the admission procedure to comply with 10:44A-4. The operative text was not read. Confirm pre-admission and admission steps from the current text.

citations.title: Changes in supports/services
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and the 2023 subchapter range. The operative text, including any transfer/discharge notice rules, was not read. Confirm before use.

citations.title: Individual Habilitation Plan (IHP)
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee has and implements a procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each individual's habilitation or service plan under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (b) The plan and monthly documentation of progress are kept in the individual's record. (c) The comprehensive IHP includes 14 elements: cover page; evaluation summaries; progress on prior goals; preferences, capabilities and needs; goals; measurable sequential objectives; method for each objective; team members and responsible persons; services with start dates, duration and frequency; barriers; guardianship review; meeting summary/addendum (disagreement may be noted); attendance sign-off; and authorization for approved individual expenses.

citations.title: Subchapter 5 - Health and Safety
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8 per the LII table of contents. A DHS 2/14/2023 webinar says 5.1(g)8-9 added a CPR mask and protective gloves to first aid kit requirements. The 2005 text had 5.1 General health care and 5.3 Over-the-counter medications. The rest of the subchapter text was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement (health care, OTC medications, food/diets, restraint/behavioral supports, incident rules) before citing it individually.

citations.title: Prescription medication
citations.requirement: (a) Individuals self-administer to the extent possible, as determined by the planning team, documented in the record and following licensee procedure. (b) If the individual cannot, the licensee or designee assists and supervises administration as prescribed. (c) A record is kept of all medication administered, including individual's name, date and medication name. For PRN medication the label must show name, date, medication, dosage, interval, maximum amount per 24 hours, stop date where appropriate, and conditions for giving it. An Advanced Practice Nurse may prescribe (2023 amendment).

citations.title: Subchapter 6 - Fire Safety and Physical Environment
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 6.1 to 6.17 per the LII table of contents. Rule text seen indicates the licensee must obtain documentation of any required Fire Official inspection and registration with the Department of Community Affairs, and a certificate from the local enforcing authority (or documentation that none is issued). The individual section text, including drill frequency, was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement before citing it individually.

citations.title: Manual of Standards for Community Care Residences (scope exclusion)
citations.requirement: Owner-occupied Family Care/Skill Development living arrangements are licensed under 10:44B and not 10:44A. This manual covers provider-managed homes and apartments only.

citations.title: Notice of Readoption, N.J.A.C. 10:44A
citations.requirement: 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (new expiration February 17, 2033). DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary. The section text cited here is the 2023-amended text, so recheck against the current rule each year.

citations.title: Enhanced Human Services enforcement authority over developmental disability providers (Jan 2026)
citations.requirement: Expands DHS enforcement authority over DD providers. The statute text was not reviewed, so counsel should read the penalty provisions.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care/home health services. NJ applies it to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange. A Live-In Worker Attestation allows exclusion where the worker lives with the person served.

citations.cite: NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115); HCBS Statewide Transition Plan Addendum #3
citations.title: Authority for DDD Supports Program / Community Care Program
citations.requirement: DDD services are authorized under the 1115 demonstration (no longer 1915(c) since Nov 2017). NJ's HCBS settings transition plan applies to 10:44A homes.

citations.cite: DDD - Apply to Become a Provider
citations.title: Combined Application / Individual Supports provider approval
citations.requirement: Agencies that want to run a licensed residential setting submit the Combined Application and select Individual Supports. At least 24 months of documented direct-care service history is required, including survey/audit results and plans of correction.

citations.title: Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report
citations.requirement: An annual financial statement audit is required for agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. The audit follows GAAS. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30).

citations.cite: DDD Division Update, January 22, 2026; iRecord Rate Change (1/1/2026)
citations.title: DSP/DSP Supervisor wage pass-through
citations.requirement: Rates for nine agency-provided services rose 1/1/2026. Agencies must pass through about $0.46/hr as a base-wage increase to DSPs and DSP Supervisors no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.

citations.cite: NJ DHS Office of Licensing (OPIA) provider page
citations.title: Inspections, provisional licenses and enforcement posture
citations.requirement: Annual and unannounced inspections, which increase beginning 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Housing must be cleared with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquisition.

citations.cite: DDD FFS FAQ: Becoming a Medicaid Provider
citations.title: Medicaid approval before billing
citations.requirement: An agency must be Medicaid-approved to submit claims for DDD services, and the same Combined Application is used for Medicaid and DDD approval. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: The manual opens with a statement of philosophy, values and goals (10:44A-2.2(b)1).
Table of organization shows lines of authority, responsibility and communication (2.2(b)2).
Licensee or executive director must meet 2.5(a): bachelor's degree, 5 years progressive DD management (2 supervisory at a senior level), and program, staff-development and fiscal knowledge.
Use the 10:44A-1.3 defined terms: governing authority, community agency head, executive director.
Document who acts as in-charge staff and who holds final authority when the executive director is absent.

policies.title: Licensure, Certification and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: No person may own or operate a community residence without Office of Licensing authorization (1.4(j)).
Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider plus Attestation for Individual Supports Provider; select Individual Supports.
Community residence: up to 16 individuals; supervised apartment: up to 4 per apartment; not on the grounds of or adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population.
Full license up to 1 year; the authorization to operate definition covers operation past expiration when inspection is delayed.
A Medicaid ID is required before billing. Owner-occupied Family Care or Skill Development is 10:44B, outside this manual. 10:44A was readopted 2/17/2026, so recheck the text annually.

policies.title: Program Description, Table of Organization and Job Descriptions
state_specifics: The program description is submitted to obtain the license. It describes services and staff coverage that assures supervision to every individual per the service plan.
The program description is reviewed in licensing inspections and amended as necessary.
After the procedure manual is approved, submit job descriptions for every position on the table of organization to DDD for review and approval (1.4(i)2).
Submit the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing for approval before opening (1.4(i)1).
Update the table of organization and job descriptions when positions change, and resubmit as DDD directs.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control (Procedure Manual Standards)
state_specifics: The licensee develops and implements the written procedure manual (2.2(a)); 2.3 governs implementation (confirm its text).
Review every procedure annually and revise as necessary (2.2(a)1).
Design every procedure on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, consistent with the organizational structure (2.2(a)2).
Each procedure has: a unique descriptive title; a purpose; sequential steps; staff responsibilities at each step; reporting and recording requirements (2.2(a)3.i-v).
Keep a revision log and recheck against the 2026 readopted text and any 58 N.J.R. 1193(b) follow-up rulemaking.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Written plan on how data is collected, analyzed and used to find patterns and systemic problems (2.2(b)22.i).
Gather input from individuals, family members and others (22.ii).
Keep a written summary of satisfaction surveys and a written summary of outcomes assessments (22.iii, 22.iv).
Action plan based on the analysis of the above (22.v).
Feed incidents, deaths, grievances, medication errors and inspection citations into the review. Mortality review follows the HW-05 death procedure.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing, EVV and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Fee-for-service: bill only after services are delivered. Reconcile claims to DDD authorizations monthly.
Do not admit anyone expecting billing until the Medicaid ID is active.
EVV through HHAeXchange for DDD Individual Supports. Live-In Worker Attestation only where the worker truly lives with the person served.
Confirm procedure codes, units and rates with DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov. Do not rely on an assumed rate.
Services are authorized under the NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115) (no longer a 1915(c) waiver).

policies.title: Annual Audit, Fiscal Sustainability Report and DSP Wage Pass-Through
state_specifics: Annual financial statement audit (GAAS) is required at $350,000 or more combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement.
Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30).
Pass through about $0.46/hr base-wage increase to DSPs and DSP Supervisors effective 1/1/2026 (deadline 3/1/2026, including retroactive pay). It cannot be a bonus or used for operating expenses.
The application requires a CPA independent examination for the two most recent fiscal years with Management Letters (1.4(c)).
NJ minimum wage is $15.92/hr from 1/1/2026.

policies.title: Inspections, Plans of Correction and Enforcement Readiness
state_specifics: Annual on-site inspection plus DHS inspection without limitation or notice (1.4(k), (l)). Unannounced inspections increase beginning 2026.
Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents.
Partial compliance can lead to a provisional license. Two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal.
Respond to citations with a written plan of correction by the deadline in the notice.
P.L.2025, c.280 expands DHS enforcement authority. Have counsel review its penalty provisions.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Comply with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (10:44A-3.1(b)).
Give the Division's rights document at admission and obtain signed acknowledgments (3.1(c)).
Train and support individuals to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because of a guardian or family (3.1(d)).
Exercising rights is never a cause for retribution (3.1(a)).
NJ's HCBS settings transition plan applies to 10:44A homes. Self-advocacy support (3.3) is to be confirmed from current text.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, House Rules, Human Rights Committee and Due Process
state_specifics: Use a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A (3.1(e)).
House rules must involve the affected individuals, be necessary to promote order, and not infringe on others' rights (3.1(e); confirm 3.2 lettering).
Any individual-specific restriction needs a documented assessed need, a less-intrusive alternative tried, consent, periodic review and a sunset date in the plan.
Individuals and guardians are told how to appeal or file a grievance (see IR-03).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: At least two levels of review, the last involving the licensee or the executive director (2.2(b)13).
Individuals file without retribution (3.1(a)).
Give the written procedure to individuals, guardians and families at admission.
Log each grievance and its outcome. Feed the data into QI (GOV-05).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Include a statement on maintaining confidentiality of individuals and records as required by N.J.A.C. 10:41-2 (2.2(b)16).
Individual files are kept at the residence (2.9(b)).
Release information only with consent or as the law requires. Log disclosures.
Address electronic records, photos and any video monitoring (IR-11).

policies.title: Personal Funds Management
state_specifics: Procedure for sound fiscal management of personal funds (2.2(b)10).
Keep a written record of every financial arrangement and transaction involving entrusted funds. Individuals and guardians may see it and get copies on request (2.10).
Manage funds so benefit entitlements (SSI $994/mo in 2026) are not jeopardized. Confirm the current 2.10 subsection.
Keep individual funds separate from agency funds and reconcile monthly.

policies.title: Safekeeping of Valuable Personal Possessions and Property
state_specifics: Written procedure for safekeeping of valuable personal possessions (2.2(b)11).
Inventory valuables on admission and update at changes. Individual or guardian signs the inventory.
Individuals control and may secure their own belongings.
Document the handling of belongings at discharge or death.

policies.title: Charges, Fees and Room and Board
state_specifics: Keep a list and schedule of all charges and fees for which an individual is held responsible (2.2(b)12).
Give the schedule to individuals and guardians at admission and on any change.
Confirm with DDD what room and board may be charged against SSI ($994/mo in 2026) before setting any charge.
Individuals may see their financial records on request (2.10).

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Use the 10:44A-1.3 definitions of guardian and fiduciary capacity.
Rights are not limited because an individual has a guardian or family (3.1(d)).
IHP includes a guardianship review (4.3(c)).
Obtain consent for medical treatment, medications, behavior support plans and photo or media release. Support decisions in accessible formats.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: No license issues if there is a final finding of discrimination (1.4(n)).
The licensee's purposes and a description of services are available to individuals, guardians, advocates and the public (2.1(a)).
DSPs must be able to communicate with the individuals they support (2.5(d)).
Provide interpreters, language access and accessible formats at no cost.

policies.title: Exchange of Contact Information with Families and Guardians
state_specifics: Written procedure for exchanging contact information with parents, actively involved family members or guardians who choose to, under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6 (2.2(b)19).
Orientation includes training consistent with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6 (2.6(a)8).
Honor the individual's preferences and guardianship status.
Record each exchange in the record.

policies.title: Video and Audio Monitoring in Common Areas
state_specifics: Procedure required if video/audio monitoring is used in common areas (2.2(b)21).
If none is used, state so in the manual.
Never monitor bedrooms or bathrooms. Notify individuals, guardians and staff, and involve the Human Rights Committee.
Set retention and access limits for recordings.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Admission procedure must comply with 10:44A-4 (2.2(b)15). Confirm the 4.1 steps from the current text.
Individuals are 21+ and Medicaid-eligible, enrolled in CCP, and choose the provider.
Give the rights document and fee schedule, and obtain acknowledgments, at admission.
Match the admission to the program description's supervision.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Habilitation Plan
state_specifics: Procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each IHP under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (4.3(a)).
The IHP has 14 elements (4.3(c)): cover page through authorization for approved individual expenses.
The meeting summary may note disagreement. Attendance is signed off.
The team includes the individual, guardian and responsible persons.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Monthly documentation of progress goes in the individual's record (4.3(b)).
Each objective has a method and responsible person.
Daily notes support the services billed. EVV records match schedules.
Entries are dated and signed with full name.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Support access to community activities, work and relationships of the individual's choosing.
Reflect employment and integration goals in the IHP.
Do not restrict visitors or access except through a documented rights restriction (IR-02).
Transportation supports integration (ENV-06).

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Record dates of transfer or discharge (2.9(b)).
Eviction is a defined term in 10:44A-1.3. Check notice and transfer rules in 4.2 from the current text.
Plan the transition with the team, guardian and support coordinator.
Return funds and belongings with a signed inventory (IR-05, IR-06).

policies.title: Medication Administration, Self-Medication and Staff Competency
state_specifics: Written medication administration procedures, including self-medication (2.2(b)17).
Individuals self-administer to the extent possible as determined by the planning team (5.2(a)).
Staff complete medication training and show competency before giving any medication, then annually (2.7(b)).
Record every dose: name, date, medication. PRN labels show dosage, interval, 24-hour maximum and conditions (5.2(c)).
Advanced Practice Nurses may prescribe (2023 amendment).

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Feeding-tube duties are delegated to nursing (2.7(d)).
No 10:44A nurse requirement was verified. A nurse consultant is a recommended practice, so confirm with the Office of Licensing.
Verify professional credentials for employed or contracted professionals (2.5(f)).
Coordinate appointments, follow-up and records with physicians.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Specialized training within 90 days: feeding techniques, mobility devices and transport, seizure and physical/medical needs, mental health needs and behavior support plans (2.7(d)).
At least one person on each shift has each required specialized training (2.8(b)).
Keep individual risk plans for seizures and choking in the record.
Confirm health care requirements in 5.1 and OTC rules from the current text.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care (Danielle's Law)
state_specifics: Call 9-1-1 for any life-threatening emergency, per Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq., and N.J.A.C. 10:42A (2.2(b)6).
Orientation includes life-threatening emergency training from the Division curriculum (2.6(a)7).
First aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant provider within 90 days of hire (2.7(a)).
First aid kit includes a CPR mask and protective gloves (5.1(g)8-9, per DHS 2023 webinar).
Report to DDD per the reportable incident rules (BEH-04).

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Treat any death as a reportable unusual incident (BEH-04). Confirm DDD timelines.
Call 9-1-1 per Danielle's Law unless a valid DNR order applies.
Notify guardian and family promptly. Secure the person's belongings and funds.
Hold an internal mortality review and send results to QI (GOV-05).

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Behavior support plan is a defined term in 10:44A-1.3.
Staff train on behavior support plans within 90 days (2.7(d)).
Use person-centered, least restrictive methods (2.2(a)2).
Review plans with the Human Rights Committee and guardian.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Confirm the 10:44A-5 restraint and behavioral support provisions from the current text before finalizing.
Any restraint use is an unusual incident and is reported (BEH-04).
Review by the Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A (3.1(e)).
Prohibit seclusion and any punitive or convenience use, and train staff on alternatives.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Include a written statement expressly prohibiting abuse, neglect or exploitation (2.2(b)8.i).

Include a written statement of the obligation to report each allegation per the statutes cited at 2.2(b)8.ii (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.10 and 52:27G-1 et seq.) and Department policy. The rule prints '9:68.10', so verify.
Preventing abuse and neglect is part of orientation (2.6(a)2) and the 90-day basic training (2.7(a)).
Abuse, exploitation and falsification are defined in 10:44A-1.3.
DDD's published issues line is 800-832-9173. Confirm the current abuse reporting number with DHS.

policies.title: Reportable Unusual Incidents
state_specifics: Procedure for reporting all unusual incidents, including but not limited to abuse, neglect and exploitation (2.2(b)8).
Orientation covers unusual incident reporting and investigating (2.6(a)3).
Confirm current DDD incident categories and reporting timelines.
Record in the incident log and in the critical information log (REC-03).
Review the data in QI (GOV-05).

policies.title: Investigations
state_specifics: Written procedure for investigations (2.2(b)9).
Protect the individual first. Separate the accused from contact pending the outcome.
Cooperate with the Department, law enforcement and DCF as required.
Document findings, corrective action and follow-up.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Treat a missing person as an unusual incident (BEH-04).
Call 9-1-1 and notify the guardian right away.
Keep a current photo and description in the record. Include elopement risk in the IHP.
Link to the emergency coverage and on-call procedure (STF-09).

policies.title: Residential Environment, Siting and Accessibility
state_specifics: Residence not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population (1.3).
Consult DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquiring housing.
Keep local enforcing authority certificate, fire official inspection and DCA registration documentation (subchapter 6).
Subchapter 6 spans 6.1 to 6.17. Confirm each section from the current text.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Evacuation Plan and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Plan for major emergencies requiring evacuation, such as a fire or gas leak (2.2(b)5).
Orientation covers the evacuation plan, emergency medical treatment, emergency coverage and on-call, fire alarm operation and fire extinguisher use (2.6(a)4).
Drill frequency is in subchapter 6 (6.1-6.17). Confirm it from the current text.
Keep drill records and review them after each drill.

policies.title: Indoor Temperature and Utility Failure Emergencies (No-Evacuation)
state_specifics: Procedure must address emergencies where evacuation may not be required, such as indoor air below 68°F or above 82°F for four consecutive hours (2.2(b)5.i).
Monitor and record indoor temperature during outages.
Have alternate heating, cooling and relocation arrangements.
Record the event as an unusual incident where applicable (BEH-04).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: First aid kit includes protective gloves and a CPR mask (5.1(g)8-9).
Staff TB screening applies (STF-05).
Bloodborne pathogen program: exposure control plan, training and hepatitis B vaccine offer.
Set illness reporting, isolation and cleaning routines.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Confirm food and diet rules in subchapter 5 from the current text.
Feeding techniques training within 90 days (2.7(d)).
Individuals choose meals. Modified diets follow written orders.
Keep choking-risk plans (HW-03).

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Staff who transport must pass driver abstract checks.
Training on mobility devices and transport within 90 days (2.7(d)).
Vehicle insurance, maintenance and inspection records are kept.
Emergency and incident procedures apply in vehicles.

policies.title: Staffing, Supervision and In-Charge Designation
state_specifics: Keep a written schedule of at least two weeks at each residence with full staff names, on-site coverage per the program description, and an in-charge employee for each shift (2.8(a)).
Agency temp staff may be in charge only if all 2.7 training is done and a written policy states licensee responsibility and liability.
Staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs (2.8(d)).
No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A. Set staffing to the program description and each IHP.

policies.title: Background Checks, Central Registry and Child Abuse Registry
state_specifics: Procedure assuring compliance with the Central Registry (2.2(b)3).
Procedure assuring no employee is on DCF's Child Abuse Registry, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-73 et seq. and 9:6-8.10f (2.2(b)20).
Agency head and owner/licensee clear criminal history checks under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69 before pay or contract (1.4(b)).
Check all employees who may contact individuals before hire.
Keep clearance records in personnel files for inspection.

policies.title: New Employee Orientation and Checklist
state_specifics: The checklist includes at least all of 2.6(a)1-8: philosophy and services; abuse, neglect and exploitation prevention; incident reporting and investigation; emergency procedures; DD overview and individual needs; job description, personnel and drug testing policies; life-threatening emergency training; N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6 training.
Confirm the text of 2.6 before finalizing the checklist.
Both the employee and trainer sign and date each item.
Complete orientation before unsupervised work.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Training
state_specifics: Within 90 days of hire: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, and first aid/CPR from an ECC-compliant entity, with certificates on file (2.7(a)).
Medication training and competency before giving medication, then annually (2.7(b)).
Specialized training within 90 days (2.7(d)).
Training records: curriculum or plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, kept in the administrative office (2.7(e)).
Run a tracker with each hire date and 90-day deadline.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: TB screen (Mantoux 5 TU PPD or IGRA blood test) within one year before or upon starting work. Written results go to the licensee.
The 2005 text required annual repeat testing. Confirm the current interval.
Applies to all employees who may contact individuals.
Keep results in personnel files.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep for each employee: application, ID and education proof, background and registry clearances, TB result, training and first aid certificates, orientation checklist, and professional credentials (2.5(f)).
Training records are kept in the administrative office (2.7(e)).
Inspectors review staff files and credentials.
Keep a signed job description in each file.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Falsification is a defined term in 10:44A-1.3. Prohibit falsifying records, including EVV and schedules.
Prohibit financial dealings with individuals and any abuse, neglect or exploitation (see BEH-03).
Staff may not retaliate against anyone who exercises rights (3.1(a)).
Orientation covers personnel policies (2.6(a)6).

policies.title: Controlled Dangerous Substance Testing of Employees
state_specifics: Written procedures assuring compliance with employee testing for controlled dangerous substances under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 (2.2(b)18).
DDD-approved providers also run pre-employment and random testing.
Orientation covers the drug testing policy (2.6(a)6).
Positive results lead to removal from duty per policy.

policies.title: Emergency Coverage and On-Call Procedures
state_specifics: Written emergency coverage and on-call procedures (2.2(b)7).
When no individuals are present, staff need not be on site, but trained paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies (2.8(c)).
Post the on-call roster and contact numbers at each residence.
For supervised apartments, staff office location fits supervision needs and response time (2.8(e)).

policies.title: Staff Qualifications, Hiring Standards and Credential Verification
state_specifics: DSP: 18 or older, high school diploma or equivalent, able to communicate with the individuals and to provide the required direct assistance or training (2.5(c)-(e)).
Residence supervisor: high school diploma or equivalent plus one year of DD experience (2.5(b)).
Executive director: bachelor's degree, 5 years progressive DD management, and program and fiscal knowledge (2.5(a)).
Verify required professional credentials for staff and contractors (2.5(f)).
Job descriptions are approved by DDD (1.4(i)2).

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep an individual file for each person. Group home and supervised apartment files are kept at the residence (2.9(a)-(b)).
Contents include full name, DOB, sex, SSN, Medicaid/insurance numbers and admission, transfer and discharge dates.
The IHP and monthly progress documentation are in the record (4.3(b)).
The retention period was not found. Confirm it with the Office of Licensing and DDD, and keep Medicaid records per DDD rules.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Unusual incident reports to DHS/DDD (BEH-04).
Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report (GOV-07).
Application and license submissions to the Office of Licensing, with plans of correction for citations.
Verify current reporting deadlines in DDD updates and the 2026 readopted text.

policies.title: Internal Communication and Critical Information Log
state_specifics: Keep a procedure for internal communication, separate from individuals' records, including a separate log of critical information and the licensee's follow-up action (2.2(b)14).
Each entry is dated and signed with the full name of the staff person (2.2(b)14.i).
Supervisors review the log each shift and document follow-up.
Do not put the log in the individual's file.

documents.title: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2 Development and maintenance of procedure manual (Standards for Community Residences for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities)
documents.form_number: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2 (no separate policy checklist form found)
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Human Services, Office of Licensing (Office of Program Integrity and Accountability)
documents.version: Text last amended 55 N.J.R. 171(a), eff. 2/6/2023. Chapter readopted without change to this section, eff. 2/17/2026 (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)), expiring 2/17/2033.
documents.how_used: Primary source. It lists the documents and procedures the licensee's procedure manual must contain. N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i) says the Office of Licensing approves the manual if it meets 10:44A-2.2. I did not find a separate Office of Licensing policy checklist form. The official PDF at nj.gov could not be fetched, so the text comes from the Cornell LII copy of the N.J.A.C. text.

documents.title: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.6 Orientation
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Human Services, Office of Licensing
documents.version: Amended 55 N.J.R. 171(a), eff. 2/6/2023; chapter readopted eff. 2/17/2026
documents.how_used: Section 2.2(b)4 requires the New Employee Orientation Checklist to include at minimum 2.6(a)1 through 8, so those items are listed as sub-items.

documents.title: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4 Application for licensure (procedure manual submission and program description)
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Human Services, Office of Licensing / Division of Developmental Disabilities
documents.how_used: Gives the submission sequence. After the application is approved and before a residence opens, the applicant submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing. After the manual is approved, the applicant submits job descriptions to DDD.

required_items.text: The licensee shall develop and implement a manual of written procedures to ensure that the service delivery system complies with State law and rules governing community residences for individuals with developmental disabilities.
The procedures shall be reviewed annually and revised as necessary.

Each procedure shall be designed in accordance with the principles of normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction, person centered planning and shall be consistent with the organizational structure and management philosophy of the licensee.
A descriptive title which is unique so as to permit easy reference and retrieval of each document;
An explanation regarding the purpose of the document;
A description of sequential steps required to successfully complete a task or action;
Assignment of staff responsibilities at each step in the implementation; and
Reporting and recording requirements for each person involved.
A statement of philosophy, values and goals so as to govern the organization's direction and character;
A table of organization that illustrates lines of authority, responsibility and communication;
A procedure for assuring compliance with the Central Registry;
A New Employee Orientation Checklist, which shall include, at a minimum, all requirements at N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.6(a)1 through 8;
The organization's philosophy, goals, services and practices;
The prevention of abuse, neglect and exploitation;
Unusual incident reporting and investigating procedures;

Emergency procedures as identified in the procedure manual; for example, the emergency evacuation plan, emergency medical treatment, emergency coverage and on-call procedures, the operation of the fire alarm system, and use of fire extinguishers;
An overview of developmental disabilities and any special needs of the individuals being served, for example, medical or behavioral problems requiring specific, tailored training;
The appropriate job description and the personnel policies of the organization, including its drug testing policies;
Training in life-threatening emergencies through a curriculum developed by the Division; and
Training consistent with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6.
A procedure for implementing a plan to deal with major emergencies requiring evacuation from the residence, such as a fire or a gas leak.

The procedure shall also address emergencies where evacuation may not be required, such as when the indoor air temperature is below 68 degrees Fahrenheit or above 82 degrees Fahrenheit for four consecutive hours;

A procedure for handling medical emergencies that includes the requirement to call 9-1-1 in the event of a life-threatening emergency, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq. (Danielle's Law), and N.J.A.C. 10:42A;
Emergency coverage and on-call procedures;
A procedure for reporting all unusual incidents, including, but not limited to:
A written statement expressly prohibiting abuse, neglect, or exploitation; and
A written statement regarding the obligation to report each allegation as required at N.J.S.A. 9:68.10 and N.J.S.A. 52:27G-1 et seq., and Department policy.
required_items.cite: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)8.ii (statute citation printed as in the source text)

required_items.text: A procedure for investigations;
A procedure to ensure sound fiscal management of individual's personal funds;
A procedure for the safekeeping of valuable personal possessions;
A list and schedule of all charges and fees for which an individual shall be held responsible;

A procedure for resolving complaints and grievances of individuals that has a minimum of two levels at which the grievance shall be heard, the last of which involves the licensee or the executive director;
A procedure, separate from individuals' records, for internal communication, to include the use of a separate log to document critical information and the action taken by the licensee to follow-up:
Each log entry shall be dated and signed with the full name of the staff person making the entry;
A procedure for admissions that complies with the requirements at N.J.A.C. 10:44A-4;
A statement regarding maintaining confidentiality of individuals receiving services and records, as required at N.J.A.C. 10:41-2;
Written procedures for medication administration, including procedures for self-medication;
Written procedures for assuring compliance with the requirements for testing employees for controlled dangerous substances, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5;

Written procedures for the exchange of contact information of parents, family members who are actively involved in ensuring the individual's welfare, or guardians who choose to, as set forth at N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6;
A procedure for assuring that no employee is included on the Department of Children and Families' Child Abuse Registry, as set forth at N.J.S.A. 30:6D-73 et seq., and 9:6-8.10f;
A procedure to address the use of video/audio monitoring in the common areas of the residences, if applicable; and
A continuous quality improvement system to identify opportunities to improve services and/or supports and to resolve identified problems. The system shall include, at a minimum:
A written plan to identify how data is collected, analyzed, and utilized to determine patterns that identify process or systemic problems requiring further in-depth review;
Input from a variety of sources, including persons receiving services, family members, and others;
A written summary of satisfaction surveys;
A written summary of outcomes assessments; and
An action plan based upon an analysis at (b)22i through iv above.

Upon approval of the manual, the applicant shall submit job descriptions to the Division of Developmental Disabilities for each position included on the table of organization in the procedure manual, for review and approval.

"Program description" means a document submitted to obtain a license from the Department. A program description includes a description of services provided to individuals and staff coverage that assures supervision to every individual served at the program, in accordance with their service plan, and is reviewed as part of the licensing inspection process. The program description is amended, as necessary.
required_items.cite: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3 (definition, quoted from the 2/5/2024 version of the chapter PDF)

sections: 2.2(a) General requirements for every procedure (annual review; normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction, person-centered planning; required elements i-v)
2.2(b)1-22 Documents and procedures to be in the procedure manual, in the regulation's own numbered order
2.6(a)1-8 New Employee Orientation Checklist content (required by 2.2(b)4)

official.notes: No official Office of Licensing policy checklist form was found. The regulation itself is the review standard. N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)1-22 is the enumerated list of required manual contents. Sequence under 10:44A-1.4: (1) The applicant starts with the DDD Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider and the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (2) The application must be complete within 45 days. The Department decides within 60 days. (3) After approval and before opening a residence, the applicant submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing, which approves it if it meets 10:44A-2.2. Licensees already operating residences with approved manuals are exempt. (4) After manual approval, the applicant submits job descriptions for every position on the table of organization to DDD for review and approval. Organize the manual in the numbered order of 2.2(b)1-22 so a reviewer can map each procedure to a citation. Each procedure should have a unique descriptive title, a purpose statement, sequential steps, staff responsibilities at each step, and reporting and recording requirements (2.2(a)3.i-v). Review the manual annually. Other subchapters (3 rights, 4 admission and service plans, 5 health and safety including medication, 6 fire safety and evacuation) set content that the procedures must follow. They are cross-referenced by 2.2(b)15 and 2.2(b)17, but I did not list them item by item because 2.2(b) is the enumerated list. The 1.4(c)1 application contents (table of organization, curricula vitae, owner and financial documents and similar) are application paperwork and are excluded, apart from the program description and the table of organization, which also appears in 2.2(b)2. The readoption notice (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)) says further rulemaking may be needed, so check the Office of Licensing site for later amendments.
